record.claim: Lu et al. (2020) create matched pairs by flipping gendered words while preserving grammatical and semantic correctness, under the definition that an unbiased model should consider each sentence in a pair equally
record.quote: creating matched pairs by flipping gendered (e.g., "he" and "she") or definitionally-gendered (e.g., "king" and "queen") words, while preserving grammatical and semantic correctness, under the definition that an unbiased model should consider each sentence in a pair equally.
record.section: 5.1.1 Data Augmentation. Data augmentation techniques seek to neutralize bias by adding new examples to the training data that extend the distribution for under- or misrepresented social groups, which can then be used for training.

record.quote: Bordia and Bowman (2019) alternatively obtain the gender subspace B from the singular value decomposition of a stack of vectors representing gender-opposing words (e.g., "man" and "woman"), and minimize the squared Frobenius norm of the projection of neutral embeddings, denoted $E(W)$ , onto that subspace with the regularization term given by Equation 35.

record.quote: Kaneko and Bollegala (2021) similarly encourages hidden representations to be orthogonal to some protected attribute, with a regularization term (Equation 36) summing over the inner products between the embeddings of neutral token $w \in W$ in an input sentence $S \in S$ and the average embedding $\bar{a}_{i}$ of all encoded sentences containing protected attribute $a \in A$ for an embedding E at layer i.
